subject.title: fix(agents): route provider-local-service health probe through fetchWithSsrFGuard

question: Should provider local-service health probes trust only loopback, RFC1918 IPv4, and IPv6 ULA literals under strict guarded fetch, or must configured local DNS, tailnet, CGNAT, unspecified-bind, or redirecting health URLs remain supported before merge?
rationale: The code path is bounded and tested, but it changes an operator-configured readiness URL from plain fetch to fail-closed SSRF policy, so maintainer intent is needed for the upgrade and security boundary.

options.title: Accept literal-private boundary
options.body: Proceed with the current policy after owner review, accepting that non-literal private health URLs may fail closed unless separately supported later.

options.title: Broaden compatibility first
options.body: Require explicit policy support and tests for any additional local URL classes maintainers consider supported before merge.

options.title: Pause for wider SSRF design
options.body: Hold this PR until exact-host trusted-origin semantics are settled alongside related SSRF work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100835.

recommendation.title: Accept literal-private boundary
recommendation.body: Proceed with the current policy after owner review, accepting that non-literal private health URLs may fail closed unless separately supported later.

likelyOwner.reason: `vincentkoc` has the strongest recent signal across provider local-service maintenance and the nearby guarded-network behavior this PR changes.
